CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  November 8, 2021 - 4:30 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  The meeting was convened and held virtually by videoconference/teleconference.

OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the meeting to order at 4:34 p.m. The pledge
  of allegiance was led by Michele Beal Bagneris, City Attorney/City
  Prosecutor.

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
 Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Andy Wilson
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember John J. Kennedy
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Felicia Williams

  Staff:  City Manager Steve Mermell
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

CEREMONIAL MATTERS  Mayor Gordo invited the community to the City's recognition of
  Veterans Day on the steps of City Hall, on Thursday, November 11,
  2021 , to honor those who have served in the military.

PUBLIC COMMENT  The following individuals advocated for the City Council to move
  forward with the rezoning of land owned by churches to allow for
  "by-right" development as a way to increase affordable housing in
  the City:

  Jill Shook, Pasadena resident, spoke on the need for the City to
  address corporate investor owned properties by creating a citywide
  policy that helps homeowners and renters; and advocated for the
  City to adopt the "The Parent Project" program for gang intervention.

  In response to public comments made by Ms. Shook,
  Councilmember Kennedy asked her to submit information on "The
  Parent Project."

  Council member Hampton requested that the Pasadena Police Body
  Worn Camera Policy be agendized at a future Public Safety Meeting
  for discussion.

  In response to Councilmember Hampton's request for an update on
  SB9 - Housing Development and the process of disciplinary action
  for Police Department personnel, Mayor Gordo responded that
  related to S89 he is considering agendizing the matter under closed
  session for City Council consideration, and disciplinary action
  process for the Police Department will be agendized at City Council
  in January 2022.

  FINANCE COMMITTEE: PURCHASE ORDER TO MERIDIAN
  DEFENSE GROUP FOR ARCHER ANTI-VEHICLE BARRIERS
  NOT-TO-EXCEED $249,244
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find this action is exempt from the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines Section
  15061 (b)(3), Review for Exemption;
  (2) Authorize a purchase order, without competitive bidding
  pursuant to City Charter Section 1002(F), contracts for labor,
  material, supplies, or services available from only one vendor, with
  Meridian Rapid Defense Group for 34 Archer Anti-Vehicle Barriers
  and 2 haulers for an amount not-to-exceed $249,244;
  (3) It is further recommended that the City Council grant the
  proposed purchase and exemption from the competitive selection
  process pursuant to Pasadena Municipal Code (PMC) Section
  4.08.049(8), contracts for which the City's best interests are served;
  and

Council Minutes  3  11/08/2021
   (4) Amend the Department of Transportation's Fiscal Year 2022
  Operating Budget by appropriating $249,244 for the purchase order
  with Meridian Defense Group. (Budget Amendment No. 2022-13)

  Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, reported that one letter expressing
  concerns with outdoor dining and safe bus access was received by
  the City Clerk's Office, distributed to the City Council, posted on-
  line, and made part of the public record for the item.

  In response to Councilmember Hampton's inquiry related to Metro's
  complaints and community bus access in the City, Steve Mermell,
  City Manager, responded that he is not aware of any complaints but
  will follow up with METRO.

  FINANCE COMMITTEE: AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO
  CONTRACT AMENDMENT NO. 3 TO THE INTERAGENCY
  AGREEMENT WITH THE LOS ANGELES COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY IN THE AMOUNT OF $103,667 IN
  MEASURE H FUNDS FOR THE HOMELESS INCENTIVE
  PROGRAM
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the recommended action is exempt from the
  California Environmental Quality Act ("CEQA") pursuant to State
  CEQA Guidelines per Section 15061(b)(3), the "common sense"
  provision that CEQA only applies to projects that may have a
  significant effect on the environment;
  (2) Authorize the City Manager to approve and execute Contract
  Amendment No. 3 to the lnteragency Agreement and all
  agreements, amendments, other related documents, with Los
  Angeles Community Development Authority (LAGOA) to receive
  Measure H Funds for the Homeless Incentive Program (HIP) in the
  amount of $103,667 for twelve months. Neither Competitive Bidding
  nor Competitive Selection are required pursuant to City Charter
  Section 1002(H) and Pasadena Municipal Code Section
  4.08.049(A)(3), contracts with other governmental agencies;
  (Contact No. 22,928-3)
  (3) Amend the Fiscal Year 2022 Operating Budget by recognizing
  revenue and appropriating $103,667 in Measure H Funds in the
  Other Housing Funds (238); and (Budget Amendment No. 2022-14)
  (4) Authorize the City Manager to approve and execute
  subsequent amendments to the lnteragency Agreement, or to enter
  into new lnteragency Agreements, to receive additional Measure H
  funds for the HIP in a total amount not-to-exceed $350,000 over the
  next three fiscal years (FYs 2023, 2024, and 2025).

MOTION:  It was moved by Vice Mayor Wilson, seconded by Councilmember
  Kennedy, to approve all items on the Consent Calendar, with the
  exception of Item 1 (Amend Existing Purchase Order No. 1220746
  with California Metro Patrol & EMS LLC), which was discussed
  separately:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Hampton, Kennedy, Madison,
  Masuda, Rivas, Williams, Vice Mayor Wilson, Mayor
  Gordo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

CONSENT ITEMS  AMEND EXISTING PURCHASE ORDER NO. 1220746 WITH
DISCUSSED SEPARATELY  CALIFORNIA METRO PATROL & EMS LLC TO PROVIDE
  SECURITY SERVICES AT THE JACKIE ROBINSON
  COMMUNITY CENTER
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the proposed action is not a project subject to the
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Section
  21065 of CEQA and Sections 15060(c)(2), 15060(c)(3), and 15378
  of the State CEQA Guidelines and, as such, no environmental
  document pursuant to CEQA is required for the project;
  (2) Authorize amendment to Purchase Order No. 1220746 with
  California Metro Patrol & EMS LLC (California Metro Patrol),
  increasing the value by $118,580 from $24,999 to a revised not-to-
  exceed amount of $143,570 and extend the term through June 30,
  2022; and
  (3) Grant the proposed amendment to the purchase order with
  California Metro Patrol an exemption from the Competitive
  Selection process set forth in the Competitive Bidding and
  Purchasing Ordinance pursuant to Pasadena Municipal Code
  Section 4.08.049(8), contracts for which the City's best interests are
  served. Competitive bidding is not required pursuant to City Charter
  Section 1002(F), contracts for professional or unique services.

  Brenda Harvey-Williams, Director of Parks, Recreation and
  Community Services, provided information on the current security
  services at Jackie Robinson Community Center, and responded to
  quest.

  Councilmember Hampton advocated for security services at all City
  parks, and requested that the matter be agendized at a future Public
  Safety Committee meeting for an update and discussion.

Council Minutes  5  11/08/2021
   Councilmember Kennedy spoke in support of the staff
  recommendation and other necessary actions to increase safety at
  Jackie Robinson Park and Recreation Center.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Kennedy,
  seconded Councilmember Hampton, to approve the staff
  recommendation:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Hampton Kennedy, Madison,
  Masuda, Rivas, Williams, Vice Mayor Wilson, Mayor
  Gordo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

Brief  Reports  From Councilmember Hampton spoke on the Rose Bowl Operating
Representatives/Requests for Company's (RBOC) event "Head in the Clouds Festival," an Asian
Future Agenda Items  music festival held on November 6-7, 2021; and advocated for the
  City Council to analyze event contracts in order to ensure that event
  promotors comply with the noise frequency of "C" and not "A." He
  also praised the City's Fire and Police Departments, and RBOC
  staff for their work in safely handling and maintaining the large
  crowd.

  Councilmember Kennedy reiterated his request to agendize under
  City Council closed session, consideration and discussion of the
  City's City Manager Recruitment.

  Mayor Gordo responded that he and staff are cognizant of the
  issues raised by Councilmember Kennedy related to the City
  Manager recruitment process, and the matter will be agenized at a
  future City Council meeting for further consideration.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Kennedy,
  seconded by Councilmember Williams, to place the City Manager
  Recruitment process on the November 22, 2021 closed session
  agenda for discussion:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Hampton Kennedy, Madison,
  Masuda, Rivas, Williams, Vice Mayor Wilson, Mayor
  Gordo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None
